title: Divergent Lazy-Initialization and Caching Mechanics
pattern: Implementing identical behavioral idioms (like lazy-initialization or local caching) using multiple distinct syntactic styles across different structs.
why_bad: It introduces arbitrary syntactic variation that obscures meaning. In a consistent system, difference in code style should signal a difference in intent. Arbitrary variation forces readers to analyze whether one method has unique safety, borrowing, or re-entrancy guarantees.
detection: Scan for lazy-initialization logic (checking for `None` then assigning `Some(val)`) and flag instances where some methods use manual `if self.x.is_none()` branches and others use idiomatic standard library combinators like `get_or_insert_with` or `OnceLock`.
counterexample:
Standardizing on different techniques because of concrete semantic requirements (e.g., using thread-safe `OnceLock` vs. single-threaded `Option`):
```rust
static GLOBAL_DATA: OnceLock<Data> = OnceLock::new();
```
fix: Standardize all single-threaded lazy caching on the most idiomatic standard library combinator.
